item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. There is real evidence of IMF- and World Bank-backed macro correction and some targeted crisis support, but the dominant 2024 picture is high inflation, FX/reserve stress, rising unemployment and poverty pressure, and a July crisis handled with curfew, shutdowns, and blame-shifting rather than clear, honest adjustment.

**Accepted Claims**
- **[IMF Executive Board Concludes the Second Review under the ECF/EFF/RSF for Bangladesh](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf)** | IMF | June 24, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh had already undertaken exchange-rate realignment and other corrective actions; the IMF still described major vulnerabilities, but this is the strongest evidence of evidence-based stabilization rather than denial. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.7

- **[Bangladesh Receives $900 million World Bank Financing to Increase Economic and Urban Resilience for Sustainable Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth)** | World Bank | June 21, 2024 | Claim: the Bank backed fiscal and financial-sector reforms, tax changes, and resilience spending to improve macro stability and shock absorption. Positive, but it is reform intent more than proof of successful outcomes. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.7

- **[World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co)** | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh and partners funded health, nutrition, education, roads, shelters, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities, which is concrete crisis-response capacity for a long-running shock. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.8

- **[UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024)** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | Claim: after floods and Cyclone Remal, UNFPA delivered targeted services to women, girls, indigenous communities, transgender people, and sex workers, showing some inclusive disaster response. This is positive but partner-led and not strong evidence of Hasina’s personal competence. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.8

- **[Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r)** | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | Claim: inflation, a balance-of-payments deficit, FX reserve pressure, import restrictions, and banking stress were already eroding purchasing power and investment. This is strong evidence that macro management was under strain. | QIDs: 5B.9

- **[Factbox: Troubled Bangladesh’s economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation](https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1)** | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | Claim: under Hasina, Bangladesh saw a widening current-account deficit, taka depreciation, falling reserves, a $4.7 billion IMF bailout, and stagnant job growth with millions of young people out of work or out of education. This is the clearest negative evidence on competence. | QIDs: 5B.9

- **[Bangladesh shuts offices, imposes curfew to curb deadly job quota protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-studentled-protests-spiral-3527920)** | Reuters | July 20, 2024 | Claim: the government responded to protests with office closures, curfew, army deployment, and communications disruption after heavy fatalities. That looks like crisis escalation, not competent or transparent management. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.7

- **[Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153)** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | Claim: Hasina publicly blamed political opponents for the violence and kept the curfew in place. That is direct scapegoating and weak evidence of honest correction. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.7

- **[Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672)** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | Claim: the Bank projected slower growth, rising extreme poverty, and more than one Gini point of increased inequality, with jobs and revenue mobilization still unresolved. This undercuts any claim that 2024 was fairly or competently managed across classes and regions. | QIDs: 5B.9, 5B.8

**Search gap**
- I found no strong 2024 evidence of a sanctions shock for Bangladesh, so the meaningful cases here are inflation, FX/reserves, unemployment, debt/IMF dependence, climate/disaster response, and the July protest crisis.
- The strongest positive evidence is mostly technocratic reform and partner-led crisis support, not proof that Hasina personally handled the year’s shocks honestly or well.
